findings.title: Denial cache key collides across resource and folder boundaries
findings.body: The denial key concatenates user, action, resource name, and parent folder with underscores but does not encode or escape component boundaries. Distinct checks can therefore produce the same key (for example, name `a_b`, parent `c` versus name `a`, parent `b_c`). Once one check is denied, the other is denied without consulting current permissions. Use an unambiguous encoding or structured hash for the key so unrelated authorization decisions cannot share a denial entry.

findings.title: Denial cache omits identity type
findings.body: The denial cache key uses `UserUID` but not `IdentityType`. User and service-account subjects can have the same UID while resolving to different permission sets, and anonymous/render identities can also reach this check with their own identifiers. A denial produced for one identity type will then immediately deny another identity type with the same UID, bypassing its permission evaluation. Include the identity type in the denial-cache key.

findings.title: Denial cache omits namespace identity dimensions
findings.body: The cache key uses the namespace string, but authorization scope can distinguish namespaces that share a value across different tenant/stack contexts if that value is not globally unique. A cached denial can consequently be reused in another authorization namespace. Key the denial by the complete parsed namespace identity (or a stable tenant identifier), consistent with the other authorization caches.

findings.title: Permission lookup errors in the cache path are silently discarded
findings.body: When `getCachedIdentityPermissions` returns an error other than a cache miss (for example, a database failure resolving user identifiers), this branch treats it like a miss and continues to `getIdentityPermissions`. That second lookup can mask the original failure or duplicate expensive work; if the repeated lookup succeeds inconsistently, the request proceeds despite the failed cache-path identity resolution. Only fall back on `cache.ErrNotFound`; return other errors as the previous direct lookup path did.
